transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-11-10
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: John Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (CTO - Stellarex), Priya Kumar (Eng Lead), Sam Lee (PM), Ben Torres (Infra)

Summary (auto): quick Optimize walkthrough focused on batching and prefix/KV cache with example cost calculations. Customer cares about p95 latency for payment authorizations and predictable unit economics.

[00:00:05] John Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, quick intros - I'm John, AE on the account, with Maya our SE.
[00:00:12] Maya Singh: Hi all, thanks for having us. We'll do a quick run through of Redwood Optimize - batching and caching, and then run a small cost model with your traffic shapes.
[00:00:25] Alex Rivera: Great, thanks. We're primarily evaluating for the payments auth path - needs very low p95, around 100 to 150ms, and cost is obviously important at scale.
[00:00:39] Priya Kumar: for context, we see spikes around end of day settlement windows and we have a lot of short prompts, like 40 to 120 tokens.
[00:00:50] Maya Singh: Perfect - those are exactly the patterns where prefix caching + batching matter. I'll start with batching basics then show how KV cache/prefix caching reduces repeated compute for similar prompts.
[00:01:12] Maya Singh: (screen share) okay, first slide: batching - continuous batching in Redwood groups concurrent requests to increase GPU utilization, we tune target batch size and max latency tradeoffs. You can set per-route batching policies.
[00:01:40] Priya Kumar: quick question - when you say target batch size, does that increase p95 because you hold requests?
[00:01:45] Maya Singh: good question. We use adaptive thresholds, e.g., target batch 32 with max wait 20ms - so small increase in queuing but much lower per-token cost. You can bias policy for latency-critical routes.
[00:02:05] John Park: we usually recommend latency-first for auth route and cost-first for background tasks.
[00:02:12] Alex Rivera: OK, demo us the prefix cache thing - not sure I'm fully visualizing.
[00:02:18] Maya Singh: sure - prefix cache / KV cache keeps token key-value state for repeated prefixes. Example: if your prompt is always the same system+user context and only the transaction details change, the shared prefix is cached so subsequent requests skip early layers of compute.
[00:02:43] Ben Torres: is that state stored in memory on the serving pool? how do you handle eviction?
[00:02:49] Maya Singh: yes it's in-memory on the inference nodes, we expose TTL and max-entries knobs and automatic LRU eviction. For Dedicated, you can configure larger cache sizes per GPU.
[00:03:05] Sam Lee: any concerns about data residency or PII in cache?
[00:03:09] John Park: good flag - Redwood provides configurable redaction at ingest and you can opt out of caching for PII-heavy routes. Also for Private deployments customers can manage KMS and audit logs.
[00:03:25] Alex Rivera: we definitely need SSO + audit logs for any PII work - we'll want security docs.
[00:03:30] John Park: we'll share SOC2 and security pack after the meeting.
[00:03:35] Maya Singh: back to cost model - slide: basic per-token model. Two knobs: effective tokens per request and cache hit rate. If your cache hit rate goes from 0% to 40% for short prompts, cost drops substantially because fewer tokens recomputed.
[00:04:05] Maya Singh: example: 100k reqs/day, avg 80 tokens, with batching vs no batching we see 30-50% cost reduction; add prefix cache hit of 30% and another 20-30% drop depending on model variant.
[00:04:28] Priya Kumar: are those numbers based on open models or Redwood verified benchmarks?
[00:04:33] Maya Singh: a mix - verified benchmarks across our catalog and on-customer pilot numbers. We'll include spreadsheet with assumptions.
[00:04:40] John Park: (note) we'll tailor to your tokenization and prompt shapes once you share sample traces.
[00:04:52] Alex Rivera: about dedicated vs hosted - latency guarantees matter, but we'll need predictable throughput during big settlement spikes.
[00:05:02] Maya Singh: Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and you can set autoscale/burst. Hosted can still be low-latency but dedicated reduces noisy neighbor risk and lets you increase KV cache size.
[00:05:18] Ben Torres: what's the typical hit on latency p95 when using prefix cache?
[00:05:24] Maya Singh: usually it reduces p95 because you're avoiding repeated compute on the prefix; however some cache lookups add a millisecond or two. Net effect for many flows is lower p95 and much lower variance.
[00:05:40] Sam Lee: we also want to understand degradation modes - what happens if cache eviction misses spike?
[00:05:47] Maya Singh: Redwood has automatic fallback to warm start (recompute) and routing policies to move traffic to different model variants if needed; we recommend canarying cache policies.
[00:05:58] John Park: moving into the live cost spreadsheet - (screen) here's a simple model: inputs are requests/day, avg tokens/request, batch efficiency multiplier, and cache hit rate.
[00:06:20] Maya Singh: example row: 1M requests/month, avg 80 tokens, batch gains 1.6x, cache hit 35% => token equivalents drop and cost per 1M tokens reduces by ~37% vs naive.
[00:06:35] Alex Rivera: are you modeling the additional memory cost for larger KV caches on dedicated?
[00:06:40] Maya Singh: yes we include a small infra premium for Dedicated instances and a per-GPU memory allocation line item in the sheet.
[00:06:48] Priya Kumar: can we see the expected CPU/GPU usage pattern during a spike?
[00:06:52] Maya Singh: yes, that'll be in the benchmark report. For short prompts, throughput is often limited by kernel dispatch latency rather than raw token compute. Batching smooths that.
[00:07:08] John Park: quick pause - any blockers that would stop you from running a pilot?
[00:07:15] Alex Rivera: security sign-off and sample traffic export are the main ones. Also want to validate cost numbers against our 6-month forecast.
[00:07:24] John Park: understood. We'll send security docs and the spreadsheet, and you send sample traffic.
[00:07:30] Maya Singh: now a short deep-dive into cache tuning - recommended TTLs: 5 to 30 minutes depending on how often prefixes change; for auth flows short TTLs like 1-5 min if you have per-user variability.
[00:07:48] Ben Torres: does Redwood support per-route cache policies? we need different behavior for auth vs analytics.
[00:07:53] Maya Singh: yes per-route policies, and route-level overrides for batch size and cache enablement.
[00:08:05] Sam Lee: what about multi-region and cross-region cache replication?
[00:08:09] Maya Singh: we don't replicate cache across regions by default - we keep caches local to reduce latency; routing policies can send traffic to a warm region if desired.
[00:08:22] Alex Rivera: competitor question - how does this differ from Anthropic's managed endpoints?
[00:08:26] John Park: main diff is production-focused knobs: per-route batching, KV cache control, and unit-econ tooling in Optimize. Teams sometimes use Anthropic/OpenAI for model quality, but Redwood focuses on predictable serving and cost controls.
[00:08:44] Priya Kumar: request: can you send a brief doc on when to use prefix cache vs. full session cache?
[00:08:50] Maya Singh: yes, we'll include that in the KB pack.
[00:08:55] John Park: (screen) quick demo of console: route config, set batch policy, enable prefix cache and set TTL. I'll show the p95 dashboard afterwards.
[00:09:10] Maya Singh: note: for debugging we surface token-level latency breakdowns in the traces so you can see whether kernel dispatch or attention layers are the bigger cost.
[00:09:26] Alex Rivera: can you run a short benchmark on our sample and show p95, median, cost delta?
[00:09:30] Maya Singh: yes, that's our standard POC step - we run a 24h synthetic replay of your traces in a sandbox and produce a report. It usually takes 48 hours to complete.
[00:09:44] Sam Lee: timeline question - if we start next week when can we get results?
[00:09:48] John Park: if you send traces by Tue (2027-11-17) we can start and have an initial report by Thu or Fri (2027-11-19/20).
[00:09:58] Alex Rivera: sounds good. Security follow-ups: SSO, KMS, audit logs - who owns that packet?
[00:10:05] John Park: John Park will share the security pack; for Private we can do customer-managed KMS, for Dedicated we support KMS integration and audit logs out of the box.
[00:10:20] Ben Torres: one more infra question - do you have a recommended model quantization level for short tokens to maximize throughput?
[00:10:26] Maya Singh: we usually recommend 4-bit for the majority of production under memory constraints but test for quality regression; Optimize will suggest quantization profile per workload.
[00:10:40] Priya Kumar: any gotchas we should watch for when enabling prefix caching in early tests?
[00:10:44] Maya Singh: watch for cache key pollution - ensure your prompt templating extracts stable prefix keys and don't include session-specific fields. Also monitor hit-rate and eviction churn in the dashboard.
[00:11:02] John Park: ok let's capture next steps - I'll send the pricing and cost model sheet, Maya to share KB items, Stellarex to send traces.
[00:11:12] Alex Rivera: agreed. Also can you include a short runbook for rollback if cache changes cause regressions?
[00:11:18] Maya Singh: yes we'll attach a rollback checklist.
[00:11:25] Sam Lee: last question - what kind of SLA do you offer for Dedicated?
[00:11:29] John Park: Dedicated contracts have an SLA with uptime and latency targets in the enterprise addendum. We'll include the SLA summary in the docs.
[00:11:40] Alex Rivera: perfect, thanks everyone.
[00:11:44] John Park: thanks folks - we'll follow up with the items discussed.
[00:11:48] Priya Kumar: thanks, bye.

(Transcript continues with Q&A, some cross talk, interrupts)

[00:28:12] Maya Singh: (answering a deep technical Q) so the KV cache stores layer-wise kv pairs, when you get a cache hit you bypass the early attention compute which is the heavy piece for short prefixes so you save a lot.
[00:31:05] Ben Torres: if we go Dedicated, any recommended memory sizing for our projected 10M req/month?
[00:31:12] Maya Singh: rough ballpark is X GB per GPU per 1M active prefixes; we'll compute exact numbers in the spreadsheet - depends on prefix length distribution.
[00:38:20] John Park: final recap: deliverables: pricing + cost model, security pack, KB notes on prefix vs session cache, your sample traces and confirm success criteria. We'll schedule the benchmark follow-up for 2027-11-19.
[00:38:45] Alex Rivera: sounds good, appreciate the thoroughness.
[00:38:50] John Park: thanks all.

End of meeting.
